failures.criterion: The round-2 fix's own contract: a role started into a kept drifted pod runs degraded — without the secrets broker — until the update round replaces its pod. Its environment must say what its start command says.
failures.evidence:
RED TEST: packages/daemon/internal/runtime/sandbox/drift_launch_env_test.go, TestAKeptPodWithoutTheEnrollmentTellsItsRoleOfNoBroker, committed at 673b49cecfc2 on legion/INFRA-484. Command: `cd packages/daemon && go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox -run TestAKeptPodWithoutTheEnrollmentTellsItsRoleOfNoBroker -count=1 -v`. FAIL at head 14f7992d.

Observed: the kept pod's generation is started with no agent-secrets flags, which is the fix working, and with `AGENT_SECRETS_URL="https://secrets.internal.example"` and `AGENT_SECRETS_KEY_DIR="/var/run/legion/agent-secrets"` in its environment, while its pod mounts no `agent-secrets-key-tester` and no `agent-secrets-token`. The two variables are gated on `r.agentSecrets != nil` (manifest.go:1108-1111) where the flags are now gated on `l.enrolls(r)` (launcher.go:433), so the one place the fix did not reach is the environment.

Why it matters: those two variables are how an agent decides it holds a broker at all — `skill://legion-worker` has a role read exactly `AGENT_SECRETS_URL` and `AGENT_SECRETS_KEY_DIR`, then run `agent-secrets <SECRET> -- <command>`, before it reports a resource unreachable. A role in a kept pod reads them, finds a key directory its pod does not mount, and reports a secrets problem, when the real state is a pod waiting for its update round. The fix's own comment says the role 'runs without the broker until the update round replaces its pod' (launcher.go:412-415); the environment contradicts it.

The fix is one line in a file this pull request already changes: gate the two variables on the launch's own `enrolls`, as `launcherCommand` does. The no-deferrals rule puts it in this pull request.

I ran the control in a detached clone of main at e4c9ab857e35 under /legion/scratch/tmp/main-control: internal/launcher (TestStartRefusesAResumeWithNoURLFile, TestAResumeIsToldWhetherItsWorkspaceWasRecreatedSinceTheTableWroteItsSession), internal/admit, internal/intake, internal/workflow, internal/natsauth and internal/testnats (panic: rootless Docker not found), internal/daemon's TestBootReconcileHoldsATodoUnderAnUnreleasedChildOfALiveTree (same panic), internal/runtime/tmux (tmux not on PATH) and cmd/legion's TestProbeImageReadsEachRolesOwnOverlaysAsTheRoleStarts, whose two subtests and message are identical on both sides. None is this change's.

The architect's second half of item 3, a session-store move: read, not a regression. A role started into the kept pod reads OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE=/var/run/legion/providers/OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN, which the old pod projects from the old key, so it works in the old store; after the replacement it reads the new store, where the launcher refuses the resume naming the session the table lacks ('resume session <file>: the session table holds no such session', internal/launcher). That is R8's reported-missing, and it was the outcome before this change too, when the launch replaced such a pod at once.

A kept pod whose enrollment moved rather than being absent (another audience, another token expiry) does not deadlock: carriesEnrollment reads volume presence alone (addresses.go), so the start keeps the flags, whose paths exist, and the shim starts; the broker then refuses the old audience and ensureEnrolled logs it without failing the transition ('It never fails a transition: a refusal is logged with its code', internal/supervise/secrets.go:76-77, 103-116). The role runs, pushes and answers its round. Read, not run: no surface here reaches a live broker.
ciAtHead: CI ran on nothing of round 2, and that is this round's second finding, recorded here rather than as a failure because my own push answers it. `gh pr checks 2538` says 'no checks reported on the legion/INFRA-484 branch'; `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/<sha>/check-runs` answers total_count 0 for all three round-2 commits (42fd726465b2, bf37eb37c435, 14f7992d73b4), and the commit status of the code head bf37eb37 is state pending with zero statuses. The cause is in the push: its head 14f7992d ends with `skip-checks: true` while the push also carried the two code commits, so GitHub started no run for any of it, and the push cancelled the one run that was in flight — run 40989912519, event pull_request at my round-1 head 4d0048de, whose `changes` job had succeeded and whose lint, typecheck, test, contracts and envoy-plugin jobs were all cancelled at 03:17:26Z. A handoff-only push takes the trailer; a push that also carries code must not, which is why my own push of this round carries red tests and no trailer, so CI starts on a head that contains the round-2 fix. I did not wait for it: a lane still running is read as running.
